requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly verified before and after restart with UID/GID 501, /home/appworker, /bin/bash, and correct home ownership.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: Persistent soft and hard nofile/nproc settings were present, and fresh PAM login sessions directly reported 8192/8192 and 256/256 both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after execution. The native account, PAM, and limits mechanisms functioned correctly without an OS, kernel, or package change.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart account, limits, SSH service, and filesystem; restart was acknowledged; the boot ID changed from fedda702-6b0d-4dd4-8000-000000000000 to 24ffacec-8e70-4f7b-8000-000000000000; and the account, limits, SSH service, filesystem, OS, and kernel were recovered and reverified.
limitations: The legacy lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command and therefore does not independently establish package consistency; however, its identical before/after result and the absence of package-management mutations provide no evidence of package damage.
Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on this legacy platform; SSH recovery was instead directly verified through the native service command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Required mutations were limited to creating appworker, adding its limits, and performing the mandatory restart. One unnecessary residue remained: cmd-276014d617764737 redirected reboot output to /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, and the final lifecycle snapshot confirms that file was not removed. No other unnecessary state-changing action is evidenced; failed discovery attempts and restart polling did not show mutations.
